text: Alex: heads up — customers hit gRPC streaming stalls for long model transfers in us-west-2 since the midnight deploy. saw multiple pods stuck on open streams :frowning:
messages:
Alex: heads up — customers hit gRPC streaming stalls for long model transfers in us-west-2 since the midnight deploy. saw multiple pods stuck on open streams :frowning:
Maria: ugh, same here. graphs show token output frozen but connection remains ESTABLISHED. tail shows repeated send errors in the runtime: "sendmsg failed: EMSGSIZE"
Chris: EMSGSIZE screams MTU/GSO/GRO mismatch. any overlay changes in the deploy? vxlan/encap adjustments?
Tara: rollback of the network-agent was attempted at 00:30 but we put it back since canary looked fine. @Chris can you run an iperf between the affected nodepair?
Chris: ran quick throughput test: iperf3 localhost -> remote gave lots of fragmentation logs on the remote node dmesg:
```
Fragmentation needed but DF set.  mtu: 1500
TCP: request_sock_TCP: Possible SYN flooding on port 9000. Sending cookies.
```
Maria: nodes show NIC MTU=9000 but vxlan0 MTU=1450 on those nodes (encap overhead). some paths hit a host with MTU clamped to 1500 (cloud uplink). that can split big GSO segments into fragments and gRPC stream code in our runtime chokes on mid-request fragment reassembly timeouts.
Alex: do we have RDMA-enabled instances in that AZ? RDMA + ip-over-vxlan multipath can expose different PMTU per path.
Chris: yes, a couple have SR-IOV/VF and RDMA set. Observed ECMP steering: some packets go over vf0 (MTU 9000) others via tunnel (MTU 1450). result = out-of-order fragments + kernel discards.
Tara: created incident in PagerDuty. Oncall Bot: Incident INC-4567 created and pages sent to infra-oncall.
Maria: quick mitigation: disabling GSO/GRO on host NIC for affected nodes reduces large skbs so kernel won't hand down giant segments for fragmentation. commands run:
```
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off
ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1450
```
Chris: confirmed runtime logs improved after toggling off GSO on two nodes — streaming resumed. but perf hit ~15% CPU increase due to smaller skbs.
Alex: long-term fix options: 1) ensure consistent PMTU across full path (set mss/clamp on edge), 2) prefer packetsize-aware routing (pin RDMA traffic to clean fastpath), 3) change runtime to handle EMSGSIZE/retry with smaller writes.
Tara: cost/ops note — forcing MTU clamp at gateway may affect throughput and bump egress cost for some heavy customers. need product signoff.
Chris: also found a kernel quirk: when SR-IOV VF has GSO and outer tunnel strips headers differently, TCP segmentation offload can produce segments larger than inner path MTU; upstream bug reports mention gRPC streaming stalls in Java/C++ runtimes with EMSGSIZE on send.
Maria: filed GH issue with repro steps and a small test harness that sends large gRPC server streaming chunks in a loop across mixed-MTU nodepairs. link: https://stash.redwood/s/infra/mtu-repro
Alex: next actions: (1) identify all nodepairs with MTU mismatch via automated probe (run traceroute -F + pmtud probe), (2) schedule controlled maintenance to clamp MTU on gateways in affected AZ, (3) add runtime fallback to chunk on EMSGSIZE and retry, (4) roll network-agent that reintroduced encap change back to previous config for now.
Tara: @DevOps Bot — can you kick off the probe job for us-west-2 and create a CSV of mismatched nodepairs?
DevOps Bot: probe job started: job_id=job-2026-03-18-01, expecting results in ~8m. output will be uploaded to /incidents/INC-4567/pmtu-scan.csv
Chris: reminder — be careful touching RDMA instances. if we disable GSO there, RDMA performance tanks. recommend migrate heavy RDMA jobs to non-multipath nodes first.
Maria: agreed. doing a targeted rollout: disable GSO on non-RDMA nodes first and collect telemetry.
Alex: thanks team. keep updates here. if streams reappear after fix, escalate to kernel-team and consider backporting net fixes to our custom kernel images. :thumbsup:
